intro: Searching for the best mortgage adviser near me usually means you want someone local you can talk to about a mortgage, whether you're buying your first home, remortgaging or moving. You want to know who is properly authorised and how they will find a suitable deal for you. iComply introduces you to a UK mortgage adviser who can quote you directly, with quotes on application.
need_heading: What people searching for a local mortgage adviser usually need
need_lead: Most people want a straightforward conversation with a qualified adviser who can look at their situation and explain the mortgage options available to them.
needs: You are buying your first home and want help understanding how much you could borrow and what deposit you need.
You are remortgaging because your current deal is ending and want to compare what else is available.
You are self-employed or have irregular income and need an adviser who understands how to present your circumstances to lenders.
You are moving home and need a mortgage that fits the new property and your changed borrowing needs.
You want to arrange protection such as life insurance or income protection alongside your mortgage.
context_heading: Understanding 'best' and 'near me' for mortgage advice
context: There is no official ranking of the best mortgage adviser, so 'best' really means the one that suits your circumstances. Mortgage advice is regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), and any adviser or broker you use should be authorised, or be an appointed representative of an authorised firm. You can check this on the FCA register, and advisers typically hold a qualification such as CeMAP.

Being near you can be helpful for face-to-face meetings, but many advisers work remotely and cover the whole country. What matters more is whether they search the whole market or a limited panel of lenders, and how they are paid — by lender commission, a fee, or both. Brokers must tell you this before you proceed, so you can judge for yourself which adviser is right for you.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Whether you are buying your first home, moving, remortgaging or buying to let, so we can introduce you to an adviser with relevant experience.
Your approximate deposit or equity, and the price of the property you are buying or the value of your current home.
Whether you are employed, self-employed or have another income pattern, as this affects which lenders may consider you.
Any credit issues you are aware of, such as missed payments or defaults, so the adviser can discuss what may be possible.
Whether you want protection advice as well as mortgage advice, such as life cover or income protection.
Your preferred way of working — face to face locally, by phone or online — and any times you are available to talk.
questions_heading: Questions to ask the mortgage adviser
questions: Are you authorised by the FCA, and can you tell me your firm's reference number so I can check the FCA register?
Do you search the whole of the market or a limited panel of lenders?
How are you paid for your advice — by lender commission, a fee, or both — and what will that cost me?
What qualification do you hold, such as CeMAP, and how long have you been advising on mortgages?
Will you also look at my protection needs, such as life insurance or income protection, alongside the mortgage?
If I have a complaint, what is your firm's complaints procedure and when could I take it to the Financial Ombudsman Service?

faqs.q: How do I check that a mortgage adviser is properly authorised?
faqs.a: Mortgage advice is regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA). You can check on the FCA register whether an adviser or their firm is authorised, or is an appointed representative of an authorised firm. Advisers typically hold a qualification such as CeMAP.

faqs.q: Does 'near me' mean I have to meet my adviser in person?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. Many advisers work by phone or online and cover the whole country, while others offer local face-to-face meetings. You can tell iComply which you prefer when you enquire.

faqs.q: What does 'best' mean when choosing a mortgage adviser?
faqs.a: There is no official ranking of mortgage advisers. It is worth checking that the adviser is authorised by the FCA, asking whether they search the whole market or a limited panel, and understanding how they are paid. That way you can judge for yourself which adviser suits your needs.

faqs.q: What can I do if something goes wrong with my mortgage advice?
faqs.a: If you have a complaint, you should first raise it with the firm. If it is not resolved to your satisfaction, you can then take it to the Financial Ombudsman Service.

extra_heading: What to expect at a first mortgage appointment
extra: When you contact a mortgage adviser after searching for the best mortgage adviser near me, the first conversation is usually a discovery chat rather than a sales pitch. The adviser will ask about your income, deposit or equity, outgoings and any credit history, so they can judge which lenders may consider you. It helps to have recent payslips, bank statements and details of any existing mortgage to hand.

A good adviser will explain whether they search the whole of the market or a limited panel of lenders, and how they are paid, whether by lender commission, a fee, or both. They should also set out the next steps clearly, including what documents they need from you and when you can expect to hear back. This is your chance to ask about their FCA authorisation and qualification before you decide to go ahead.

Many people assume a local adviser will automatically get them a better deal, but location alone tells you little about the advice you will receive. What matters is that the recommendation is suitable for your circumstances and that you understand the costs involved. If anything is unclear, ask the adviser to explain it again before you commit.

extra_faqs.q: Will an adviser near me charge for the first meeting?
extra_faqs.a: This varies between firms, so it is worth asking before you book. Brokers must tell you how they are paid, whether by lender commission, a fee, or both, so you can decide with the full picture in front of you.

extra_faqs.q: Can I use a mortgage adviser if I have already found a property?
extra_faqs.a: Yes. An adviser can look at your circumstances and recommend a suitable mortgage even if you are already some way through a purchase. It is worth telling them early so they can discuss timescales with you and any deadlines set by the seller.

extra_faqs.q: What if I am not sure whether I need a mortgage adviser at all?
extra_faqs.a: Some people prefer to approach lenders directly, while others want someone to compare options and explain the paperwork for them. A mortgage adviser can recommend a mortgage based on your circumstances, and you can ask them to set out clearly what they will do for you before you decide.
